title: The lobby, the player list and getting ready
summary: R.E.P.O. gets a crew together in a lobby of its own: the game keeps lobby types, lists the players itself, caps the crew through its networking layer, and has a separate state for watching instead of playing.
body: Before a run there is a lobby, and the game has a menu of its own for it rather than leaving the whole thing to a platform overlay.
Lobby types are remembered. The game keeps a record of the kinds of lobby that have been saved, which is why a setup can be picked again rather than rebuilt every session.
The crew is listed by the game. There is a player list the menu can show, and the menu elements carry hover and animation states of their own, so the list is a menu object rather than a line of text.
Networking carries its own limit. The game uses a networking view of its own and keeps a maximum number of players, so the size of a crew is set by the game rather than by whoever is hosting.

Voice is carried alongside the written chat. The game includes a voice layer from the networking library it uses and has a voice box component of its own, which is a second way of talking that is not the chat box.

Being ready is a state rather than a button. Extraction has readiness flags and a localised ready label, so the game knows when the crew is standing in the right place instead of only knowing that something was pressed.
A player can also be left watching rather than playing: the game keeps a flag for spectating that is separate from being in the run.

What this entry does not tell you: how many players a crew may hold, what the voice layer does in detail, or what each lobby type changes about a run. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The game has a lobby menu and keeps the types of lobby that have been saved.
The main menu has a game mode state of its own.
The menu can list the players, with hover and animation states of their own.
Networking uses a view of its own and keeps a maximum number of players.
Voice comes through the networking library the game uses, and there is a voice box component of its own.
Extraction readiness is a state with flags of its own and a localised label.
There is a flag for a player spectating rather than playing.
The lobby has its own camera menu and buttons for stepping to the next and the previous player being watched, and it ships lobbies of its own such as a forest one.
facts.evidence: asset names: CameraLobbyMenu, Big Button Spectate Next, Big Button Spectate Previous, Lobby Forest

facts.claim: The lobby is a scene of its own, with a forest, a landscape, a ditch, a road, a wooden barrier and signs for a closed road and for no stopping.
facts.evidence: asset names: Lobby - Forest, Lobby Landscape, Lobby Ditch, Lobby Road, Lobby Wooden Barrier, Lobby Sign - Closed Road, Lobby Sign - No stopping

facts.claim: Those two signs are drawn from sheets of their own, one for the closed road and one for no stopping.
facts.evidence: asset names: Sign_Closed Road_Albedo, Sign_No stopping_Albedo
